findings.text: Public reclaim guard interface normalizes the caller mask into current context and then conditionally engages filesystem reclaim tracking only when direct reclaim is genuinely required. The acquire and release forms pair around a reclaim section, with filesystem tracking further gated on flag __GFP_FS.

Low level exclusive tracking for filesystem reclaim sections. Acquire takes exclusive ownership of the global map __fs_reclaim_map for the caller return address while release drops it. Callers pair the two and only use them after establishing that reclaim tracking applies.

Reclaim tracking applies only when the effective mask carries __GFP_DIRECT_RECLAIM, current flags lack PF_MEMALLOC, and mask lacks __GFP_NOLOCKDEP. Missing any one condition suppresses tracking entirely.

Filesystem reclaim map follows strict acquire release pairing keyed by caller address, taken only on the filesystem flagged direct reclaim path and released on the matching exit. The acquire path also briefly touches the MMU notifier range map as an acquire immediately followed by release, without holding it across reclaim.

Node reclaim is a bounded attempt to free up to a requested page count on one node, with establish, conditional reclaim and release responsibilities. Establish covers scheduling, stall, accounting, guard and per task state. Conditional reclaim applies only when thresholds indicate sufficient material and is bounded by target and priority exhaustion. Release restores guards, detaches state and reports the accumulated total.

Shrinking is skipped unless either pagecache reclaimable material exceeds threshold min_unmapped_pages or reclaimable slab counted by NR_SLAB_RECLAIMABLE_B exceeds threshold min_slab_pages. When entered, the loop continues while the accumulated total stays below target and priority stays nonnegative, with priority decreasing across iterations, so termination is assured.

Reclaimable pagecache estimate selects its base from mode flag RECLAIM_UNMAP tested in node_reclaim_mode. One mode counts all file pages tracked by NR_FILE_PAGES while the other counts only unmapped file pages. Dirty file pages tracked by NR_FILE_DIRTY are then excluded by subtraction with a clamp that prevents underflow, so the result never wraps and never exceeds the base.

Unmapped file estimate is the excess of total file LRU pages tracked by NR_INACTIVE_FILE plus NR_ACTIVE_FILE over mapped file pages tracked by NR_FILE_MAPPED, floored at zero. The floor covers accounting overlap where mapped count can exceed LRU count due to shared tmpfs pages counted in another category.

Batch uncharge accumulator groups consecutive work by owning object group. It carries the current group pointer, a node identifier, plus tallies for chargeable memory, kernel memory subset and completed output pages. A helper resets all fields to zero before a new batch.

Uncharge aggregates per folio releases into per group batches. Folios sharing the same group accumulate together while a group change flushes the prior batch and starts a new one. Single and multi folio entry points share the same accumulator and flush discipline, clearing the folio charge mark and balancing group references exactly once per batch plus once per folio.

Chargeable memory accounting distinguishes kernel charged folios, root owned folios and ordinary folios. Kernel folios increment both memory and kernel tallies with kernel tally MEMCG_KMEM. Root owned ordinary folios skip the memory tally but still count as output. Flush applies memory uncharge, kernel adjustments and legacy bookkeeping only when the corresponding tally is nonzero.

Folio charging resolves an owning group for the folio node and attempts a sized charge, committing the association on success. Variants resolve the owner from an address space, from a stored swap identifier with fallback to the faulting address space, or from current context for huge pages. Huge page and swap in paths become no operation returning success when accounting is disabled or inapplicable, with huge page exhaustion reported as out of memory.

Root level object groups bypass the sized charge attempt but still receive the commit association, so root folios are tracked without consuming a limit. Non root groups must succeed at the sized attempt before commit. On failure the temporary group reference is dropped and no association is installed.

Migration preserves group ownership across folio replacement. Same node moves reuse the source group reference directly. Cross node moves derive the counterpart group for the same memory group at the destination node and drop the source reference, returning a single owned reference in both cases.

Replacement and migration require locked source and destination with matching anonymity and size, and migration additionally requires the source off the reclaim list. Already charged destinations or missing source ownership cause early return without changes. Replacement force charges the destination only when its derived group is non root. Migration settles source counters immediately when derivation collapses a non root source to root, then transfers ownership and clears the source.

Socket ownership binds a socket to the current memory group at allocation, releases it on free, and transfers it on inheritance. Allocation is skipped outside task context, when socket accounting is disabled, for the root group, or for legacy hierarchies without per group socket activity. Inheritance is a no operation when both sockets already share the same owner. Otherwise it releases the old owner and takes a counted reference on the new one.

Socket memory charging is gated by a disabled by default static branch memcg_sockets_enabled_key. On the default hierarchy a sized charge attempt precedes the socket counter update tracked by MEMCG_SOCK and reports success or failure to the caller. Release decrements the counter and returns pages to the per group stock. Legacy hierarchies delegate both directions to separate helpers.

Default memory control table exposes per group tunables and reports. Most entries hide on the root. Read only usage, peak with open and release plus show and store, limits with show and store, event files with stored offsets plus show, always visible usage statistics with optional NUMA breakdown, delegatable group oom control and delegatable reclaim trigger are present, followed by a terminator.

Memory controller registration bundles lifecycle handlers for state allocation, online, offline, release, free, reset and statistics flush, plus task attach, fork and exit hooks. It points the default hierarchy at the memory file table and the legacy hierarchy at a separate table when that mode is built, with early initialization disabled.

Group and object group lookups that can race with teardown run under read side critical sections with online or counted references held across use. Swap charging additionally serializes the swap entry association under a per cluster lock held only for the update. No sleepable work runs while holding those critical sections.

Swap charging pins the owning group by identifier, validates that the folio is in swap cache, attempts a sized swap reservation for non root owners and records the association with its statistics. Uncharge looks up the owner by identifier and reverses the reservation and statistics. Combined accounting mode bypasses the separate swap reservation path.

Swap reservation problems are signaled through dedicated event counters rather than only by return code. Reservation exhaustion records both a limit hit and a failure event before releasing the pinned identifier and reporting out of memory. A missing cache association records only the failure event and reports success with no charge.

Early memory controller setup covers type overflow validation, dying CPU handling registration, per CPU workqueue creation, per CPU drain work initialization and slab cache creation for group and per node descriptors with node count sizing.

Boot time strings configure memory accounting features. One handler accepts a comma list selecting socket, kernel memory and BPF accounting opt outs. The other handles the legacy swap account switch by emitting a one time deprecation notice when disabled. Both report successful parsing.

Swap control files report current usage in bytes, high and maximum limits with textual maximum support, peak usage with reset, and event counts. High and maximum stores parse the same textual form but install differently, one through a dedicated setter and one through an atomic exchange. All entries hide on the root and the table is terminated.
Provides a synchronous barrier that waits until all previously queued per group background work has completed.

Several paths defend against inconsistent inputs. Build time validation rejects an oversized charge batch. Reclaim estimates clamp subtractions that could underflow. Uncharge asserts the folio is off the reclaim list and warns on unexpected deferred work. Replacement and migration validate locking, type match and size match before touching accounting.

ABI names are current, peak, min, low, high, max, events, events.local, stat, optional numa_stat, oom.group and reclaim. All but stat hide on the root, and delegation is permitted for oom.group and reclaim.
ABI names are swap.current, swap.high, swap.max, swap.peak and swap.events, all hidden on the root. Event output labels are high, max and fail. Boot tokens are nosocket, nokmem and nobpf.

Correctness depends on exact pairing. Temporary group references drop on charge failure, batch references exactly once per group run, and per folio charge marks clear only after tallying. Reclaim context requires matched guard save and restore plus matched task state attach and detach and matched filesystem tracking acquire and release. Mismatching any pair leaks accounting or tracking state.
